events.description:
The way software gets built is changing shape. For the last few years, AI helped you write code faster. Now a new category is emerging: Software Factories. Systems where AI agents don't just assist a developer, they run the full pipeline: spec, build, test, review, ship, and iterate, often with multiple agents working in parallel like stations on an assembly line.
It's one of the hottest threads in AI right now, and for good reason:
Coding agents got good enough, fast. Once agents could reliably plan, write, run, and debug code, the obvious next question became: why stop at one agent helping one person?
